Camera patches validate before mutation; unavailable captures/invalid HWND preserve authoring.
GPU-independent picking: nearest visible geometry, no-hit, top-left coordinates, true triangle/rotated-box intersections, clipping and strict atomic guards.
Framing combines visible descendants, respects aspect/clipping, preserves orientation, supports non-rendered entities and never edits world bytes.
Runtime picking/framing uses frozen geometry and hierarchy after authored deletion/reparenting without advancing ticks.
GPU-independent skin picking follows edited joint poses and excludes obsolete rest geometry.
Host destruction releases writer ownership and endpoint; frontend HWND survives; committed edits survive reopen.
limitations: Native ABI/HWND automation, not physical Avalonia widget qualification.

observations: Reuses PlayerClock and one native WorldSession runtime. Only owner poll advances automatic simulation; inspection, drawing and captures cannot step it.
Fixed 60 Hz with at most eight catch-up ticks per poll and dropped-time telemetry. Exact floating-point boundary regression also protects the standalone player clock.
Pause and resume clear fractional time. Queued capture holds automatic simulation and discards the held interval when it releases.
Manual step, audio replay and gameplay module load/edit reject during automatic playback; paused step keeps core receipt retry behavior.
Game preview stages the actual Camera before switching. Runtime lens and entity identity remain frozen after authored edits/deletion; pose follows the live runtime hierarchy.
Scene navigation and gizmos reject in Game view. Switching back retains the inspection camera.
A missing camera fails an awaiting capture immediately without poisoning graphics. A real animation sampling failure rolls back the tick batch and pauses the clock.
GUI transport observes native state, including external agent pause/resume, without per-tick Inspector/Hierarchy rebuilds. Stop retains authored revision/history.
GUI tests include the existing draft, Scene input, gizmo, floating-panel and saved-layout workflow.

An initial GUI run failed a tool shortcut assertion; diagnosis found unisolated desktop modifier state in semantic messages. Qualification now scopes explicit modifiers to the calling UI thread, restores them after synchronous dispatch, and preserves production input behavior and exact shortcut assertions.
limitations: Game view is an editor physics/animation preview; gameplay device input and audio output are not connected here. The standalone player remains the playable path.
Simulation continues while owner polling continues, including hidden/detached viewports and locked Windows sessions; no focus-based suspension is claimed.
The UI dispatcher currently polls at 33 ms and performs synchronous scene work. Fixed 60 Hz simulation does not imply 60 FPS presentation or production-scale performance.

Earlier locked-session attempts could not capture the full editor. Final qualifying runs captured the actual editor client area after Windows was unlocked; this does not establish user visual acceptance.

Owned-HWND messages and semantic actions do not qualify physical input, IME, accessibility or arbitrary multi-monitor/DPI behavior. Explicit script runs isolate interactive messages to scoped synchronous dispatch and retain genuine lifecycle events; normal editor input is unchanged.
Single active Scene/Game viewport, explicit Camera choice; no automatic camera replacement after authoring deletion.
Multiselect, rendered asset previews, complete animation/VFX authoring and the wider M0/M1/M2 qualification remain unfinished.
